seamVerdict: The seam COMPILES, RUNS and is FUNCTIONALLY CLOSED, but it carries one silent-widening hole and one redundant mechanism. Nothing here is broken; two things are untidy in a way that matters to this program's honesty standard.

seamFindings.status: CONFIRMED exactly as the contract states
seamFindings.what: src/editor/enablement.ts RegionToggleRequest declares `route?: string | null` ('the route the operator is looking at — the default disable scope'). src/editor/panels.ts RegionEnablementWriteRequest (lines 64-73) has NO `route` field. src/editor/server.ts (lines 471-481) forwards regionId/enabled/scope/routes/cascadeRegionIds/reason and NOT route. src/editor/region-enablement.ts (lines 100-109) cannot forward it because the field does not exist upstream. So request.route is ALWAYS undefined on every HTTP path.
seamFindings.workaround: src/editor/client.ts:229 sends `{ regionId, enabled, route: S.route, routes: [S.route] }`. server.ts drops `route` and forwards `routes`. enablement.ts:390 uses request.routes when defined.
seamFindings.doesTheWorkaroundFullyCloseIt: FOR SCOPE SELECTION, YES. The engine receives a single-route list, which is a PARTIAL route list, which is exactly the precondition rule 1 (shared-page-blast-radius) needs in order to fire. The refusal the design depends on is reachable. FOR THE WIDENING SIGNAL, NO — see the next finding.

seamFindings.severity: honesty gap — a guard against silent widening that is itself silent
seamFindings.what: enablement.ts:385 computes `widenedToBlastRadius = scope === 'routes' && request.routes === undefined && route === null && blastRadius.length > 1`, commented at :380 as existing 'because a silent widening is exactly the failure' to prevent, and returns it on RegionToggleResult (:284, :506). grep proves the identifier appears ONLY in src/editor/enablement.ts and nowhere else in src/ or scripts/.
seamFindings.consequence: TWO independent reasons the operator can never be told: (a) RegionEnablementWriteResult in panels.ts has no such field and region-enablement.ts's write() does not copy it, so it is dropped at the adapter even if true; (b) because client.ts always sends `routes: [S.route]`, request.routes is never undefined on the UI path, so the flag can never BECOME true there anyway. The guard is unreachable through the shipped UI and unreadable through the port.
seamFindings.notAFailure: No current behaviour is wrong: the UI always names a route, so no widening actually occurs today. The defect is that if a future caller omits routes, the widening would happen and the flag that exists to announce it would be discarded in silence.
seamFindings.recommendation: Either add `widenedToBlastRadius` to RegionEnablementWriteResult and forward it in region-enablement.ts write(), or add `route` to RegionEnablementWriteRequest and have server.ts forward body.route so the field earns its comment. Do NOT delete the flag.

seamFindings.what: `route` (singular, on RegionToggleRequest) and `routes` (array, on both request types) both express disable scope. client.ts:229 populates BOTH from the same value S.route. Only `routes` survives the server boundary. client.ts:227-228 documents this honestly: 'the single route is sent alongside it for the same intent, and is ignored where unread.'
seamFindings.consequence: A reader of enablement.ts reasonably assumes `route` is live; it is dead on every path that exists today. This is the residue of the two halves converging on the same requirement independently.

seamFindings.what: tsconfig include is ['src/**/*.ts','scripts/**/*.ts'], and the browser half lives in `export const EDITOR_CLIENT_JS = ` (client.ts:107) as a template string. So `pnpm typecheck` exit 0 says NOTHING about the correctness of the `routes: [S.route]` workaround.
seamFindings.whatActuallyProvesIt: smoke:editor-integration's 25 Playwright checks — in particular the refusal assertions 28.P8.8-28.P8.11 — are the ONLY evidence that the client sends the right body. That evidence exists and passes; the point is that the typecheck-exit-0 line must not be read as covering it.

seamFindings.what: I scanned every `export` in src/editor/*.ts and counted references across src/ and scripts/ excluding only the declaration line itself. ZERO orphaned exports. UNWIRED_REGION_ENABLEMENT is live as the default parameter at runtime.ts:95; REGION_ENABLEMENT_SEAM is live at panels.ts:130/213/267 and is the 501 body; regionEnablementRows is live at region-enablement.ts:93/112. An earlier cruder scan of mine produced 40 false positives by excluding same-file uses — I discarded it.
seamFindings.note: Every symbol client.ts and panels.ts assume exists does exist with a compatible signature — typecheck exit 0 over both files is the proof, and the adapter in region-enablement.ts is the only translation layer.

seamFindings.what: The route-enablement path (server.ts:495-510) reads body.route, body.enabled and body.reason and calls toggleRoute directly — no adapter, no dropped field. Both enablement handlers call runtime.refreshProject() and runtime.syncEnablement() only when result.changed, and return the sync alongside the result. Refusals return HTTP 200 with the refusal body, never an error status, so the client renders the engine's reason rather than 'failed'.
